name_reason: Compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ game-global prefix, battle_ core-table domain (matches every sibling summon-animation global in anisummn.c), summon_anim_variant_d domain descriptor (matches the sole accessor fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_d_3slot), and terminate_flag reflects both the datatype (a single-byte boolean latch) and the purpose (set when the animation winds down, suppresses color rotation). 'd' is a legitimate animation-variant domain label (variants a/b/d/e exist), not Ghidra address residue. Ghidra symbol and C symbol are byte-identical.
purpose: Terminate latch for the variant-D 3-active-slot summon animation; once set it suppresses the per-color rotation step during the wind-down/hold phase.
logic_summary: Single uint8 of zero-bss runtime scratch used only by fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_d_3slot. INIT (state_code 0) clears it to 0 (MOV byte ptr [0x540B8],0x0 at 0x27339) before any read this run. The state-6 hold path sets it to 1 (MOV byte ptr [0x540B8],0x1 at 0x27365). It is read byte-wide on a frame-7 even tick (MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [0x540B8] at 0x273ED, inside the frame==7 branch after CMP [color_idx slot frame]==7 at 0x273E4/0x273EB): when nonzero (TEST/JNZ 0x27425) the per-color rotation (increment+mod-10 of color_rotation_counter, copy into color_idx_array[i], reset frame counter to 0) is skipped, so the animation stops cycling colors. Never persisted; on-disk image is 0x00.
element_semantics: Scalar boolean latch: 0 = color rotation active, 1 = terminated (color rotation suppressed). Set only by the state-6 hold path, cleared only by INIT.
notes: Source comment block (anisummn.c lines 188-201) was already accurate, precise, and conclusion-style: byte single-byte latch, zero-bss, INIT clear at 0x27339, state-6 set at 0x27365, frame-7 guard read at 0x273ED with rotation skipped when nonzero, single accessor fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_d_3slot. All cited disasm addresses verified against current disassembly (the three xrefs to 0x540B8 are exactly WRITE@0x27339, WRITE@0x27365, READ@0x273ED).
